mainTopic: When two people's קרבנות פסח get mixed up, does the משנה's solution fit the view of רבי יהודה, who requires one original member of each group to stay registered?
overview: This amud opens by closing the previous case with a famous saying of the חכמים: silence is fitting for the wise, and all the more so for fools. It then turns to the משנה about two people whose פסחים got mixed up. In the משנה's solution, each original owner withdraws from his own animal and leaves an added person registered on it. The גמרא suggests this contradicts רבי יהודה, who requires that at least one original member always stay registered on a פסח. רבי יוחנן answers that the משנה can still follow רבי יהודה. Since רבי יהודה forbids slaughtering a פסח for one person alone, the owner was always expected to add a partner, so the newcomer counts like an original member. רב אשי then proves from the משנה's wording, "five groups of five each," that it really does follow רבי יהודה. The amud ends with the הדרן, closing the chapter מי שהיה טמא on פסח שני.

steps.title: Closing lesson: silence is fitting for the wise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wraps up the previous case with a lesson from חכמים, supported by a פסוק in משלי: silence is fitting for the wise, and all the more so for fools.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here the Sages said: Silence is fitting for wise people, and all the more so for fools, as it says: "Even a fool who keeps quiet is considered wise."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the previous discussion with a moral lesson. In that case, speaking up and appointing the other side caused a loss, while staying silent would have kept everything valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case, if neither side had appointed the other to slaughter on its behalf, both offerings would have been valid and eaten. Because each side spoke up and appointed the other, one animal had to be burned. The חכמים draw the general lesson that silence is often wiser, and they use a קל וחומר: if it helps the wise, it certainly helps fools.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said. A lesson is being drawn from the case just discussed.
Silence
All the more so; reasoning from a lighter case to a stronger one
Fools
A fool who keeps silent (from משלי 17:28)

steps.whatToRemember: The previous סוגיא ends with the lesson that saying less is sometimes better, because speaking up there actually caused a loss.

phrases.english: From here the Sages said:
Silence is fitting for the wise,
and all the more so for fools.
phrases.notes: If silence helps even wise people, fools certainly benefit from it.

phrases.english: As it is said:
"A fool who keeps silent is considered wise."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier סוגיא (end of 98b) about mutual appointments.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Silence would have saved both offerings in the previous case. In general, silence is wise, especially for fools.

steps.title: Quoting the new משנה: two people whose פסח offerings got mixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה about two people whose פסחים got mixed up, to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Two people whose פסח offerings got mixed up, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the heading of the משנה to show which topic it is about to discuss. This is a setup line for the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, each owner brings in an outside person to join his group. Then each original owner withdraws from his own animal and joins the other one. As a result, each animal is left registered to the outsider, who was not there when the animal was first set aside. That detail is what the גמרא will question next.

keyTerms.meaning: Became mixed up
Their פסח offerings
Etc. (the rest of the quote)

phrases.english: Two people whose Pesach offerings got mixed up, etc.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the closing lesson of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה gives a method for two people whose פסחים were mixed up, in which each original owner ends up withdrawing from his own animal.

steps.title: Does the משנה contradict רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה does not follow רבי יהודה. According to a ברייתא, רבי יהודה requires one original member of the group to remain registered, while רבי יוסי only requires that the פסח never be left with nobody registered at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה? A ברייתא teaches: "And if the household is too small for a lamb" teaches that the group may keep getting smaller, as long as one of the original members remains. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי יוסי says: as long as they don't leave the פסח by itself with no one registered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה by pointing to רבי יהודה's rule that at least one original member must stay registered on a פסח. In the משנה's solution, only a newcomer is left on each animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק as allowing members to withdraw, but only as long as one original member stays. In the משנה, both original owners withdraw from their own animals and leave behind only people added later. So the משנה seems to fit רבי יוסי, who only requires that someone, anyone, always be registered.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)
They may keep decreasing (members may withdraw)
Members of the group registered on the פסח
Provided that
As it is, meaning left alone with no one registered

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is more lenient here. He does not need an ORIGINAL member to stay, only that the פסח is never left with nobody at all. The problem in the משנה exists only according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Shall we say that our Mishnah
is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?
For it was taught in a Baraita:
"And if the household is too small for a lamb"
teaches that they may keep decreasing,
phrases.notes: Members may withdraw from the group.

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁיְּהֵא אֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה קַיָּים,
phrases.english: provided that one of the members of the group remains,
phrases.notes: This means one of the ORIGINAL members.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יַנִּיחוּ אֶת הַפֶּסַח כְּמוֹת שֶׁהוּא!
phrases.english: provided they do not leave the Pesach as it is (with no one registered)!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions which תנא the משנה just quoted follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's solution, in which both original owners withdraw from their own פסחים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה requires an original member to remain registered. In the משנה, only newcomers remain on each animal, so it seems to contradict him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the newcomer counts like an original member
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can follow רבי יהודה. Since רבי יהודה forbids slaughtering a פסח for a single person, a lone owner was always expected to add a partner, so the added person counts like an original member.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. Since רבי יהודה holds that a פסח may not be slaughtered for one person alone, from the very beginning the animal was meant to have another person registered with the owner. So the newcomer is like one of the original group members.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן defends the משנה and shows it can fit רבי יהודה after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה elsewhere rules that a פסח cannot be brought for a יחיד. So when one person set aside a פסח, the plan from day one included adding at least one more person. The person who joins later is therefore filling a place that was planned from the start, and he is treated like an original member. That satisfies רבי יהודה's requirement.

keyTerms.meaning: Even if you say (the answer works even according to this view)

keyTerms.term: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד
keyTerms.meaning: One may not slaughter the פסח for a single person
From the very beginning
To register / appoint (someone onto the offering)
Is considered like

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: a person added later can count as an 'original' member if the setup always required him to be there.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Even if you say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
since Rabbi Yehuda said

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוֹחֲטִין אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הַיָּחִיד,
phrases.english: one may not slaughter the Pesach for a single individual,
from the beginning it stood ready to register another person with him,
so he is like one of the original members of the group.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines who counts as an 'original member' according to רבי יהודה's own other ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The newcomer from outside is not an original member, so the משנה contradicts רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a lone owner was always required to add a partner, that partner counts as an original member, and the משנה fits רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב אשי: the משנה's wording supports רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי proves from the משנה's phrase "five groups of five each" that it follows רבי יהודה. If one group had only four people, the solution would fail because no original member would remain in that group.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The משנה's wording also shows this, since it teaches: "And so too five groups of five each." Groups of five, yes. But groups of five and one of four, no. Isn't that because no original member of the group would remain with it? Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings support from a precise reading of the משנה, showing it requires an original member to stay. That is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With five groups of five, each group can send four members to the other groups and still keep one original member. If one group had only four, all four would have to leave, and no original member would remain. The משנה's limit to groups of five only makes sense according to רבי יהודה. שמע מינה confirms this.

keyTerms.meaning: Is also precise (its wording supports this)
For it teaches
Yes / no
Is it not because...? (a rhetorical question making a proof)
Remains
Learn from it (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה follows רבי יהודה. A newcomer counts as an original member because a פסח can't be for one person (רבי יוחנן), and the משנה's 'groups of five' wording confirms an original member must remain (רב אשי).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The Mishnah is also precise in this way,
for it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן חָמֵשׁ חֲבוּרוֹת שֶׁל חֲמִשָּׁה חֲמִשָּׁה.
phrases.english: "And so too five groups of five each."
Groups of five, yes,
but groups of five and one of four, no.
phrases.notes: The solution would not work if one group had only four.

phrases.english: Is it not because there would not remain
one of the original group members with it?
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer that the משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי יהודה's requirement that an original member remain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's precise wording, "five groups of five each," which excludes a group of four.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows רבי יהודה. Each group must keep one original member, which is why the solution only works with groups of five.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter מי שהיה טמא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally ends the ninth chapter of פסחים, called מי שהיה טמא, and notes that the topic of פסח שני is now complete.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter מי שהיה טמא, and the topic of פסח שני is finished.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the closing line that marks the end of the chapter מי שהיה טמא, saying "we will return to you" and noting that the study of פסח שני is complete.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הדרן is said at the end of every chapter. It shows love for the learning and a hope to come back and review it. The words וּסְלִיקָא לַהּ פֶּסַח שֵׁנִי tell us the chapter's main subject, פסח שני, is now finished, so the next text will begin a new chapter.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you: the formula said when finishing a chapter
"One who was impure": the opening words and name of this chapter
And it is finished: the topic is completed
The second פסח, brought on the 14th of אייר by someone who missed the first one

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter מי שהיה טמא is complete. Its main topic was פסח שני and other problems with the קרבן פסח, ending with the case of mixed-up פסחים.
steps.confusionAlert: The הדרן is not part of the שקלא וטריא. It does not answer or prove anything. It is only a closing marker for the chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter "One who was impure"
phrases.notes: This is the usual way a chapter ends, calling the chapter by its first words.

phrases.english: and the topic of the Second Pesach is concluded

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final discussion of the משנה about mixed-up פסחים (steps 2-5).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ninth chapter of פסחים, מי שהיה טמא, which deals with פסח שני, is complete.
